original_target.title: Controlled global Coulomb gauges in ordinary Lorentz weak L4

full_original_statement:
Fix a compact Riemannian four-manifold $`(M,g)`$. For each finite $`\Lambda>0`$, does there exist $`C(M,\Lambda)<\infty`$ with the following property?

Every $`W^{1,2}`$ connection $`\nabla`$ on an $`\mathrm{SU}(2)`$ principal bundle over $`M`$, with $`\|F_\nabla\|_{L^2(M)}\le\Lambda`$, admits a global, possibly singular $`W^{1,(4,\infty)}`$ section as in Theorem A of [1], such that its connection form $`\alpha`$ satisfies

```math
d^*\alpha=0\quad\text{in distributions},\qquad
\|\alpha\|_{L^{4,\infty}(M)}\le C(M,\Lambda).
```

Here the norm is the ordinary Lorentz weak norm

```math
\|\alpha\|_{L^{4,\infty}(M)}
=\sup_{t>0} t\,\mathrm{Vol}_g\{x:|\alpha(x)|>t\}^{1/4}.
```

There is no curvature-smallness or Yang–Mills equation assumption. Singular sections are allowed; a smooth global trivialization and a prescribed singular set are not required.

sources.scope_comparison: The exact target requires ordinary Lorentz weak L4 together with distributional Coulomb condition for all finite curvature bounds, allowing singular sections. Wang's actual Theorem1.2 instead estimates the calligraphic integrability-radius space. The paragraph after Remark1.2 explicitly says this space is neither stronger nor weaker than ordinary Lorentz L4,infinity, so it does not yield the target norm. Small-energy or stationary Yang–Mills restrictions also do not cover all connections and all finite Lambda. No new complete matching announcement was found.
